name: Long-range cord forager (sparse, fast, migrates)
description: Leaves its wood as sparse, fast fans that bundle into persistent cords, thickening the routes that carry flow and recycling the rest. It can move its whole network to a large new resource.

tip_speed.note: from the type species Phanerochaete velutina: from a search snippet (8.4 mm/day); the paper was not opened (research/01-growth-biology.md [22])

growth_unit.note: as for the type species Phanerochaete velutina: no measurement for the type species; fast-explorer value suggested in research/01 section 4

branch_angle.note: as for the type species Phanerochaete velutina: no measurement for the type species; fast-explorer value suggested in research/01 section 4

branch_angle_sd.note: as for the type species Phanerochaete velutina: default from Hopkins & Boswell 2012 (79 +/- 10 deg, research/09); not measured for the type species

sensitivity.note: how strongly tips turn away from crowding; model coefficient

fusion_probability.note: fitted so that the engine gives about 1 fusion per 8 branches, as measured in Podospora anserina (research/01 [8]); not measured for this species

density_cap.note: hyphal density at which branching stops; tuning value

cord_max.note: largest cord cross-section, in single hyphae; cords of 48 to 480 um are measured (research/02) but this is a tuning value

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

degradation_rate.note: none seen in 15 h in R. solani; small value so dead hyphae clear

passive_transport.note: diffusion between neighbouring segments; measured diffusion inside hyphae (1 to 2 x 10^-9 m2/s, research/10) is several times faster than the passes allow

soil.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

wood.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

litter.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

root.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

agar.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

transport_speed.note: from the type species Phanerochaete velutina: solute velocity in cords 20 to 100 mm/h, rising with cord development; the low end is used (research/10-fricker-2017.md)

t_opt.note: as for the type species Phanerochaete velutina: extension rises with temperature from 5 to 20 or 27 C (research/08 [14])

wobble.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

avoidance.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

fusion_probability.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

uptake.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

turn.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

spike_interval.note: default; no recording for any member of this family (research/04)

spike_duration.note: default; no recording for any member of this family (research/04)

spike_amplitude.note: default; no recording for any member of this family (research/04)

score.note: Phanerochaete velutina replaced Hypholoma fasciculare and Trametes versicolor and deadlocked only with Stereum hirsutum (research/06 section 2.5 [4]); combat rank rises with extension rate (research/06 [2][3])
